title: Infinity Yoneda and pointwise mapping-space limit calculus
statement:
Use the infinity categories and universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and the mapping-space and coherent-diagram conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Write $\mathcal S$ for the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small spaces. It admits all $\mathcal U$-small limits. For every infinity category $\mathcal E$ fitting in $\mathcal U'$ and having $\mathcal U$-small mapping spaces, the infinity categories $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E,\mathcal S)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ admit $\mathcal U$-small limits, computed objectwise (the functor categories themselves may be large relative to $\mathcal U$). More generally, for a small simplicial set $K$ and an infinity category $\mathcal V$, every small limit or colimit diagram in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal V)$ is characterized objectwise whenever the corresponding limits or colimits exist in $\mathcal V$. In particular, when $\mathcal V$ has all small colimits, colimits in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal V)$ exist and their source and target are the corresponding colimits in $\mathcal V$. The Yoneda functor $j:\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$, $j(e)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(-,e)$, is fully faithful.

For every small coherent diagram $p:J\to\mathcal E$, a cone with apex $l$ is limiting if and only if its induced maps $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,l)\to\lim_{j\in J}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,p(j))$ are equivalences, naturally in $x$. Dually a cocone with apex $c$ is colimiting if and only if $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(c,x)\to\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(p(j),x)$ is an equivalence for every $x$. In particular, covariant representable mapping-space functors preserve all existing small limits, and contravariant representables take all existing small colimits to limits. These equivalences are natural in the diagrams and in the testing objects.

proof.text:
Let $F:J\to\mathcal S$ with $J$ small. By [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] choose its left-fibration representative $E_F\to J$ with small total simplicial set, and put $M=\operatorname{Fun}_{/J}(J,E_F)$. This is a small Kan complex: it is the mapping complex over $J$ from the identity left fibration to $E_F$, and in each degree it is a subset of the set of maps between two small simplicial sets. For a small Kan complex $X$, the same classification, its constant-functor clause and the exponential identity of simplicial sets give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal S)}(\Delta_JX,F)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{/J}(J\times X,E_F)=\operatorname{Fun}(X,M)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(X,M).$$
The last comparison is the classification over a point, which identifies its mapping complex with maps between Kan complexes. These comparisons are natural in $X$. Write $\Phi_X$ for the displayed equivalence from transformations to maps into $M$, and choose $\lambda:\Delta_JM\to F$ with $\Phi_M(\lambda)\simeq1_M$. For $a:X\to M$, naturality and composition compatibility give $\Phi_X(\lambda\circ\Delta_Ja)\simeq\Phi_M(\lambda)\circ a\simeq a$, on the entire mapping space. Since $\Phi_X$ is an equivalence, composition with $\lambda$ is its inverse and is therefore an equivalence. The limiting-cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes this a limit. For $J=\varnothing$ the section complex is a point, so the construction includes the terminal object.

source.place: Limits-of-spaces construction, section-space model; comparison with arbitrary constant Kan-complex diagrams

proof.text:
Fix small $J$, a simplicial parameter $K$ in a sufficiently large universe, and a diagram $P:J\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal V)$. Currying, given degreewise by rearranging the factors $J\times K\times\Delta^n$, gives $\widetilde P:K\to\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal V)$. Let $\mathcal D_0$ be the full subcategory of $J$-diagrams admitting a limit, and assume every $\widetilde P(k)$ belongs to it; fullness makes $\widetilde P$ factor through $\mathcal D_0$. Apply [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] with $T=\Delta_J:\mathcal V\to\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal V)$. A limiting cone is precisely a universal arrow $\Delta_J l\to Q$, by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], so the hypothesis holds on $\mathcal D_0$. Its parameter clause supplies $L=R\widetilde P:K\to\mathcal V$ and a cone $\lambda:\Delta_J L\to P$ such that, for every $A:K\to\mathcal V$,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal V)}(A,L)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal V))}(\Delta_JA,P).$$
Hence $\lambda$ is a limit by the same cone criterion, and each evaluated cone is its universal-arrow component, hence is limiting. For any other cone $\mu:\Delta_JH\to P$, this equivalence gives a comparison $u:H\to L$ carrying $\lambda\Delta_Ju$ to $\mu$. If $\mu$ is limiting, its universal property at $L$ gives $v:L\to H$ with $\mu\circ\Delta_Jv\simeq\lambda$. Then $\lambda\circ\Delta_J(u\circ v)\simeq\mu\circ\Delta_Jv\simeq\lambda$; the equivalence for $\lambda$ at $L$ gives $u\circ v\simeq1_L$. Also $\mu\circ\Delta_J(v\circ u)\simeq\lambda\circ\Delta_Ju\simeq\mu$; the equivalence for $\mu$ at $H$ gives $v\circ u\simeq1_H$. If $u$ is an equivalence, its mapping-space maps are equivalences and the cone criterion makes $\mu$ limiting. By the vertexwise-equivalence criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], $u$ is an equivalence exactly when every $u(k)$ is one; applying the preceding universal-property argument at $k$ says exactly that every $\mu(k)$ is limiting. This proves existence and the objectwise characterization without assuming that all $J$-limits in $\mathcal V$ exist, and without assuming $K$ is small in the smaller universe.

proof.text: Apply Step 2 to $\mathcal V^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $K^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversing simplicial orders identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal V)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal V^{\mathrm{op}})$ and reverses cones into cocones. Thus the same existence and recognition assertions hold for colimits. With $K=\Delta^1$, evaluation at its two vertices gives exactly the source and target colimit statements. Finally take $\mathcal V=\mathcal S$, $K=\mathcal E$ or $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$, and use Step 1: both space-valued functor categories have small limits, regardless of their larger size. Only the diagram shape $J$ and values of $F$ in Step 1 were required to be small.

source.place: Opposite and universe specializations of Step 2

proof.text:
For $p:J\to\mathcal E$ and $x\in\mathcal E$, use the source-fixed arrow left fibration over $\mathcal E$ classified by $H_{\mathcal E}(x,-)$ in [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], and pull it back along $p$. Its section complex is exactly the arrow mapping complex from $\Delta_Jx$ to $p$: an $n$-simplex is a map $J\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal E$ with source constantly $x$ and target $p$ on $J$, constant in the other factors at that endpoint. By [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] in $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)$, this is naturally equivalent to $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)}(\Delta_Jx,p)$. Apply the mapping-complex clause of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] with the constant one-point functor as source. It identifies this section complex with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal S)}(\Delta_J\Delta^0,H_{\mathcal E}(x,p(-)))$. The equivalence $\Phi_{\Delta^0}$ of Step 1 identifies the latter space with the small limit of $H_{\mathcal E}(x,p(-))$. This also covers a pulled-back arrow fibration whose total space is only $\mathcal U'$-small: it is its section space, rather than its total space, that is equivalent to the small limit model. These identifications carry postcomposition of a map $x\to l$ with a given cone to its induced compatible family, including its higher coherence. The cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore gives exactly
$$l\text{ is the apex of the specified limiting cone}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,l)\xrightarrow{\sim}\lim_J\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,p(-))\quad\text{for every }x.$$
A cocone $p\to\Delta_Jc$ is a cone in $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ on $p^{\mathrm{op}}:J^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$. Applying the proved cone test there, and identifying $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,c)$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(c,x)$, gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(c,x)\simeq\lim_{J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(p(-),x)$ exactly when that cocone is colimiting. Applying the forward directions to existing limit or colimit cones proves the two representable-preservation assertions.

source.place: Section models and the mapping-space tests for cones; the argument uses arbitrary fixed-source arrow families

proof.text:
Curry the coherent bifunctor of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] to obtain $j(e)=H_{\mathcal E}(-,e)$ and choose the equivalent right-fibration model $\mathcal E_{/e}\to\mathcal E$ supplied there and in [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. For any $F:\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$ represented by $q:E_F\to\mathcal E$, classification gives
$$\operatorname{Map}(j(e),F)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{/\mathcal E}(\mathcal E_{/e},E_F).$$
The identity vertex $1_e$ is final in $\mathcal E_{/e}$: apply [lem-coef-infinity-slice-equivalence-final] to the equivalence edge $1_e$. Thus $\{1_e\}\hookrightarrow\mathcal E_{/e}$ is right anodyne by [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-anodyne]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] to $q$ and this inclusion, and pull its displayed map back over the fixed base map $\mathcal E_{/e}\to\mathcal E$. This yields the restriction map
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{/\mathcal E}(\mathcal E_{/e},E_F)\longrightarrow(E_F)_e\simeq F(e)$$
as a trivial Kan fibration. Its lifting property survives the pullback by solving the same lifting square upstairs and retaining its prescribed base map. By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence] it is a homotopy equivalence. All these arguments may be made in $\mathcal U'$; they do not require $\mathcal E$ to be $\mathcal U$-small. Now take $F=j(e')$. The composite is evaluation at $1_e$, so its composite with the map induced by $j$ on $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(e,e')$ is $u\mapsto u\circ1_e$, naturally homotopic to the identity on that entire mapping space. Since evaluation is an equivalence, the map induced by $j$ is an equivalence. This proves full faithfulness, with the actual Yoneda map identified rather than an unspecified equivalence between the two spaces.

source.place: Yoneda by restriction of maps of right fibrations to the identity vertex of the representable slice

proof.text: The equivalences in Step 1 are the transport comparison followed by the simplicial exponential identity; Step 2 uses the specified universal-arrow transformation and its evaluation compatibility; Step 4 restricts the same arrow family and takes its section complex. Thus precomposing in the testing object, or changing the coherent diagram, commutes with these comparisons up to the coherences already supplied by transport and universal arrows. The canonical comparison of each cone with the chosen limit is defined by its own universal property, not by a choice of independent objectwise identifications. The opposite constructions retain the same compatibilities. This proves the stated naturality in diagrams and testing objects. Explicitly, for $a:x'\to x$, a family $(b_j:x\to p(j))$ restricts to $(b_j\circ a)$; for a coherent transformation $t:p\to p'$, it maps to $(t_j\circ b_j)$. The comparison of a specified cone $\lambda$ sends $f:x\to l$ to $(\lambda_j\circ f)$. These formulas commute by the composition and unit coherences in the transport node. For higher simplices use the representing simplicial mapping complexes in the transport classification: composition of simplicial maps and restriction along $\Delta^m\to\Delta^n$ commute. The coherent classification comparison carries these identities to the arrow families displayed in Step 4 and gives the corresponding coherent compatibility on spaces. No strictly chosen composition operation in $\mathcal E$ is needed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q66-155fcf1c6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes and every cited statement in full. The item statement (HTT 5.1.2.2/5.1.2.3, 5.1.3.1-2, 4.2.4) is unchanged and nothing is weakened. Only the evaluated diagrams need limits, and the different sizes (small J, large E or K, small mapping spaces) are kept apart. Step 1: sections M=Fun_{/J}(J,E_F) of a small representative are a small Kan complex. The exponential identity holds degreewise, and choosing lambda with Phi_M(lambda)~1 makes a->lambda.Delta(a) an equivalence, so the cone criterion applies; J empty gives a point. Step 2: currying gives P~:K->Fun(J,V), and D0 is the diagrams admitting a limit. By cone calculus, limiting cones are exactly universal arrows for Delta_J, so the parametric node applies. Both inverse identities and the vertexwise-equivalence argument are correct, and large K uses the stated universe enlargement. Step 3: an elementary dualization through Fun(K,V)^op=Fun(K^op,V^op), plus K=Delta^1 and V=S. Step 4: sections of the pulled-back source-arrow fibration are exactly U_{Fun(J,E)}(Delta x,p). Pinch comparison, the pullback and mapping-complex clauses of transport, and Phi_{Delta^0} identify this with lim_J Map(x,p(-)), so the cone criterion gives the claim; the cocone case goes through E^op. Step 5: 1_e is an equivalence edge, so it is final in E_{/e} (slice-equivalence-final), hence right anodyne (terminal-anodyne). The fiber of exponentiation's rho over the projection is restriction to (E_F)_e, a trivial Kan fibration and so a homotopy equivalence (08NS node). The postcomposition clause makes the composite u->u.1_e, which proves full faithfulness. Step 6: naturality bookkeeping from the stated coherence clauses. lem-coef-space-transport-classification is true straightening for left fibrations, with Kan mapping complexes Fun_{/A}(E_F,E_G) and the Hom bifunctor with its slice and arrow models. It is not a duplicate of the relative-nerve, exponentiation, slice, arrow-target, fibers or cbc Grothendieck straightening nodes. lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows is true: partial universal arrows assemble into a contractible choice, and the Fun(K,-) mapping formula follows. It strictly generalizes the unsplit total local-adjoint and pointwise-adjoint criteria, which give neither the partial domain nor the parameter formula that Step 2 needs, so it is not a restatement. The graph has no cycle (44-node closure). Both nodes have correct blueprint from/via fields and same_as=[], after a search of the main-20261015 blueprint that found no infinity-categorical Yoneda node, and all three kinds of Mathlib search; my own grep found only the ordinary 1-categorical PartialAdjoint. No SGA is used.
